messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

- [2025-01-17] standup/cinder/2025-01-17-2: For the record, the indexer is owned by Cinder.
- [2026-03-17] standup/atlas/2026-03-17: Decided in today's standup: image-resizer will keep original uploads for 90 days only, since storage for originals doubled in six months. For anything Atlas-related, page Priya.

- [2025-05-20] handover/2025-05-20-search-indexer: Team Atlas is taking over search-indexer from team Cinder, effective today. Dashboards and alerts are being repointed.
- [2025-04-03] standup/atlas/2025-04-03: Reminder from team Atlas: page Tomasz for anything this cycle, not Priya.
- [2025-06-27] handover/2025-06-27-notifier-correction: Correction to the handover note of 2025-06-11: the notification service went to the Dune team, not team Cinder. The Cinder team never owned it; the note was written against the wrong team.
- [2025-03-20] handover/2025-03-20-image-resizer: Ownership change: the image resizer now sits with team Ember. Team Dune no longer owns it.
- [2025-01-20] standup/ember/2025-01-20: The job scheduler lives with the Ember team. For the record, the authentication gateway is owned by Ember.
- [2025-01-09] standup/boreal/2025-01-09-2: The Boreal team owns the notifier.

Question: Which services does Atlas own now?

message.content: billing-api, feature-flags, product catalog, event bus, search-indexer
message.reasoning:
The question asks which services Atlas owns now (today is 2026-06-30).

Let me go through the memory entries:

- Ledger service: owned by Atlas (2025-01-08, 2025-07-17). But 2025-10-13: "From today the pager for the ledger rings Cinder, not team Atlas. Ownership transferred." So ledger is no longer Atlas — transferred to Cinder.
- Billing API: lives with Atlas team (2025-01-08). Nothing later supersedes. Also 2025-09-30 billing-api decision (still implies Atlas planning meeting context, but doesn't change ownership).
- Feature-flags: owned by Atlas (2025-01-08). Correction 2026-03-09: flags service went to team Atlas, not Dune. So Atlas owns feature-flags.
- Product catalog: Cinder owned it (2025-01-17), but 2025-12-19 handover: Atlas taking over product catalog from Cinder, effective today. So Atlas owns product catalog now.
- Event bus: 2025-11-24: Atlas taking over event bus from Boreal. So Atlas owns event bus.
- Search-indexer: 2025-05-20: Team Atlas taking over search-indexer from Cinder. So Atlas owns search-indexer.
- Image-resizer: 2025-03-20: sits with team Ember. Not Atlas.
- Reporting service: Ember.
- Job scheduler, auth gateway: Ember.
- Notifier: Dune (correction 2025-06-27). Boreal owned notifier earlier (2025-01-09), but correction/handover 2025-06-27 says notification service went to Dune team.
- Indexer: Cinder.

So Atlas owns now: billing API, feature-flags (flags service), product catalog, event bus, search-indexer.

The rule says: "When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for... and nothing else." So one short line listing the services.

Answer: billing-api, feature-flags, product catalog, event bus, search-indexer.
